items_missed: Hourly rate per mover per hour never stated — only a dollar range
What's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools) never listed
Number of movers and trucks never stated with the estimate
Traffic not named as a variable despite quoting a two-hour arrival window
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing
No mention of the BOLDED detail list at the top of the confirmation email
Never asked customer to review the confirmation email and reply with corrections
Insurance explained without the 60c/lb baseline contrast
top_strength: Nicole caught a bad online estimate and fixed it on the call instead of letting it ride: "since you're moving from a third floor with a long walk, moving to a third floor with a long walk, I will estimate your move to take around five to six hours," revising the customer's own 4-hour self-booking upward and getting an explicit "Okay, yes" to it. When the customer stalled on distance — "I'm really not that good at distances" — she reached for the company equivalent instead of guessing: "we just use a typical school bus as a reference one. School bus is about forty feet long," and got a usable answer back. Clock section was perfect, and she hit both Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee verbatim.
coaching_note: She re-quoted the move upward — "It's good to budget around $1,040 to $1,248" — without ever restating the hourly rate, the mover/truck count, or what that rate includes, so the customer heard a bigger number with no value attached to it. On a call where you are raising someone's estimate, the pricing block is the thing that makes it land: two movers and one truck at the hourly rate, gas and truck and insurance and wrap and tools included, no hidden fees. Say the rate before the range, every time you revise upward.
phone_presence_notes: Efficient and pleasant with good recovery on the distance question, but heavily reliant on repeated "Awesome" transitions and no use of the customer's name, so warmth reads as scripted rather than personal.
